channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Acceptability and Experience of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Adult ADHD: A Systematic Review With Narrative Synthesis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review with narrative synthesis examined the acceptability of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for adults with ADHD, addressing a gap in understanding how core ADHD symptoms may influence treatment engagement and satisfaction. The review included 21 studies (RCTs, pilot/feasibility trials, qualitative and mixed-methods studies) and mapped findings to the seven domains of the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA).
FINDINGS: Acceptability was most consistently assessed in the domains of affective attitude, intervention coherence, perceived effectiveness, and self-efficacy. Positive drivers included skills training, psychoeducation, therapeutic support, accountability strategies, and individualisation. Burden was primarily associated with homework demands, cognitive load, and treatment intensity. Group and digital formats were generally acceptable but depended on facilitation quality, accessibility, and therapeutic presence. Ethicality and opportunity costs were rarely reported.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is heterogeneous, combining diverse study designs and measures, which limits firm conclusions. However, the synthesis suggests that CBT for adult ADHD is most acceptable when it enhances engagement, understanding, and perceived benefit while minimising burden. The review highlights the importance of intervention content and delivery style over format alone. Key limitations include the lack of standardised acceptability measures and underreporting of ethical and opportunity-cost domains.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should prioritise structured, flexible CBT interventions that incorporate psychoeducation, skills training, and accountability strategies to improve acceptability. Attention to homework load and cognitive demands may reduce treatment burden. Further research using standardised acceptability measures is needed to refine delivery approaches.

item.title: Outcomes of Mindful Mood Balance for Moms, online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depressive relapse prevention in the USA: a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic randomised clinical trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study evaluated whether adding an online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme (Mindful Mood Balance for Moms) to usual care reduces depressive relapse and symptom burden in euthymic pregnant women with recurrent depression in the USA, using a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic RCT.
FINDINGS: In 500 participants (mean age 32 years, mean 11.5 weeks gestation), MMB for Moms reduced relapse risk over 6 months postpartum (33% vs 44%; hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.56–0.99; p=0.045). Symptom burden decreased more during the 12-week intervention (average PHQ-9 reduction 0.75 vs 0.31), but not across the full trial period (0.61 vs 0.54).
INTERPRETATION: The trial suggests a modest reduction in relapse risk and short-term symptom improvement with MMB for Moms versus usual care. Strengths include pragmatic design and low attrition (77–78% follow-up). However, the effect on relapse is modest (HR ~0.74), the CI approaches 1, and symptom benefits did not persist postpartum. Funding from NIH/NIMH supports credibility, but generalisability to non-academic settings or outside the USA is uncertain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: MMB for Moms may offer a non-pharmacological adjunct for perinatal relapse prevention, particularly during pregnancy, but the clinical impact appears limited and not sustained postpartum; integration should be cautious pending replication and cost-effectiveness data.

item.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review examined whether EEG neurofeedback improves symptoms, cognition, or brain activity in adults with ADHD, comparing standard and personalised training protocols. Seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n = 390) were included.
FINDINGS: RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects on ADHD symptoms versus controls (effect sizes not reported). Non-randomised studies reported larger symptom reductions, but with high risk of bias. Cognitive gains were inconsistent and likely due to practice effects. Protocol-specific EEG changes were observed without convergence across studies. No treatment-related adverse events were reported.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by small samples, heterogeneous protocols, variable controls, and risk of bias. RCTs do not currently support efficacy over placebo. Non-randomised studies suggest potential benefit but are prone to confounding. High-quality, blinded RCTs with standardised outcome measures are needed to determine clinical utility.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: EEG neurofeedback cannot be recommended as an evidence-based treatment for adult ADHD based on current data. Clinicians should discuss this uncertainty with patients and consider established treatments while awaiting better trials.

item.title: Intravenous Ketamine for Depressed and Suicidal Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Double-Blind Trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial (n=29) tested whether a single intravenous ketamine dose (0.2 mg/kg) reduces depression or suicidality more than placebo within 3 hours in adolescents (12–17 years) with treatment-resistant depression presenting to the ED with suicidal ideation.
FINDINGS: At 1 hour, ≥50% reduction on SIQ occurred in 0% placebo vs 14.3% ketamine (P=0.48); on BYI Anxiety 0% vs 21.4% (P=0.22); on BYI Depression 0% vs 15.4% (P=0.22). At 3 hours differences were smaller. Adverse effects, notably dissociation, were more frequent with ketamine (60% vs 7%, P=0.004), resolving within 1 hour.
INTERPRETATION: The study is underpowered (n=29) and shows no statistically significant benefit of ketamine over placebo on primary outcomes. Confidence intervals are wide and include clinically meaningful effects, so a true difference cannot be excluded. The higher dissociation rate with ketamine is notable but transient. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine efficacy, optimal dosing, and safety in this population.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support routine use of single low-dose IV ketamine in suicidal adolescents in the ED. Further research is required before any practice change; meanwhile, standard care remains appropriate.

item.title: The pharmacogGENEtics in Youth Depression (GENE-YD) study for personalizing antidepressant pharmacotherapy for young Western Australians - A feasibility study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The GENE-YD study assessed whether pharmacogenetic (PGx) testing to guide antidepressant prescribing is feasible and potentially beneficial in young people (16–24 years) with major depressive disorder, using a triple-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) design comparing PGx-guided treatment to treatment-as-usual (TAU).
FINDINGS: Of 73 screened, 55 were randomized (1:1) with 39 completing baseline and 38 completing 12-week follow-up. Protocol adherence and participant satisfaction were high, and attrition was low. The PGx-guided group showed greater reductions in depressive symptom severity (effect size not reported), higher response (50% vs. TAU) and remission rates (38% vs. TAU), and improved quality-of-life outcomes at 12 weeks.
INTERPRETATION: This pilot RCT demonstrates feasibility and acceptability of a triple-blind PGx-guided antidepressant trial in youth, with preliminary signals of clinical benefit. However, the small sample (n=38 completers), lack of effect size reporting, and short follow-up limit conclusions on efficacy. The study’s strengths include robust blinding, low attrition, and strong protocol fidelity, but external validity is uncertain given the single-center, highly selected sample.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: PGx-guided antidepressant prescribing may be feasible in youth, but current evidence is insufficient to recommend routine use. Larger, fully powered trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm clinical benefit and cost-effectiveness before changing practice.

item.title: Undertreatment of Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol-related clinical contexts: a scoping review of diagnosis, thiamine regimens, and clinical management.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is a preventable neurological emergency in alcohol use disorder (AUD) that is often missed or undertreated due to diagnostic uncertainty and heterogeneous management. This scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) mapped evidence on diagnosis and thiamine regimens in AUD or clinically significant alcohol use, focusing on practice variability and undertreatment.
FINDINGS: Only 26 studies were included, with only two RCTs on thiamine regimens; no consensus on optimal dosing emerged. Diagnostic criteria varied widely, and observational studies consistently reported undertreatment, including delayed initiation and frequent use of oral thiamine in high-risk scenarios. Protocolized, guideline-concordant care was associated with earlier parenteral thiamine use in suspected/confirmed WE.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited, heterogeneous, and underpowered, with no clear optimal thiamine regimen. While diagnostic variability and undertreatment are well-documented, the strength of conclusions is constrained by the lack of high-quality trials and inconsistent diagnostic criteria. Early recognition and parenteral thiamine in high-risk cases remain plausible but unproven strategies to reduce morbidity.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should prioritize early suspicion of WE in AUD patients, use parenteral thiamine in high-risk cases, and follow local protocols where available, while acknowledging the lack of definitive evidence for optimal dosing or regimen.

item.title: Protocol for a parallel-group superiority randomized controlled trial comparing Sage- a couple psychotherapy- to supportive individual psychotherapy for borderline personality disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) carries high mortality and morbidity, and frontline treatments are often inaccessible or only partially effective. Sage is a novel, protocolized couple psychotherapy for BPD that targets both patient symptoms and relationship conflict, but its superiority over standard supportive care has not yet been tested in a rigorous trial. This is a single-blind, parallel-group RCT protocol comparing Sage to supportive individual psychotherapy in 152 couples where one partner has BPD.
FINDINGS: The trial randomizes couples to 16 weeks of Sage (couple-based) versus supportive individual psychotherapy (separate sessions for patient and partner). Primary outcome is BPD symptom change; secondary outcomes include relationship conflict and partner mental health. Assessments occur at baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-ups. Primary analysis will use intent-to-treat generalized mixed linear models. No results are reported yet.
INTERPRETATION: This is a well-designed, adequately powered RCT with masked assessors and independent supervision to prevent drift, which strengthens internal validity. However, as a protocol paper, no outcome data are available, so efficacy, effect sizes, and safety remain unknown. The design addresses an important gap—testing whether adding a relationship-focused component improves outcomes—but generalizability may be limited by the requirement of a stable intimate partner and the exclusion of individuals without one.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Until results are published, clinicians should view Sage as an experimental intervention. Standard evidence-based treatments for BPD (e.g., DBT, MBT) remain first-line while this trial is ongoing.

item.title: [Efficacy and tolerability of co-administration of clozapine with atypical antipsychotics in patients with treatment-resistant schizophrenia, comorbid with chemical addictions].
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study compared six clozapine-plus-atypical-antipsychotic combinations in 470 adults with treatment-resistant paranoid schizophrenia, 83 % of whom also had a comorbid substance use disorder. It is a six-arm, open-label RCT conducted across multiple Russian psychiatric centres (2018–2026).
FINDINGS: After 42 days, combinations with cariprazine and, to a lesser extent, lurasidone produced significantly greater reductions in positive and negative symptoms than the other four regimens (p < 0.05). The cariprazine group also had the longest subsequent outpatient treatment duration. No adverse events were attributed to the combinations.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary and of low internal validity: randomisation method and allocation concealment are not described, raters were unblinded, and no adverse-event monitoring protocol is mentioned. The 42-day horizon is short for a chronic disorder, and the lack of placebo or clozapine-monotherapy arms precludes firm conclusions about incremental benefit. Effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported, so statistical versus clinical significance cannot be judged.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings do not yet justify changing practice. Clozapine plus cariprazine may be considered on a case-by-case basis when negative symptoms dominate, but clinicians should await larger, longer, and better-controlled trials before adopting this strategy routinely.

item.title: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced people: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the prevalence of complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) in forcibly displaced populations (refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced people) and assessed whether CPTSD adds clinically meaningful information beyond classic PTSD in this group. Twenty studies (17 independent samples, n = 12,504) were synthesised.
FINDINGS: Pooled CPTSD prevalence was 20.9 % (95 % CI 12.6–32.6 %), but heterogeneity was extreme (I² = 98.3 %; 95 % prediction interval 1.7–80.3 %). Prevalence was 10.6 % in community samples versus 55.2 % in treatment-seeking samples. Asylum seekers showed higher rates than refugees. Across four studies, post-migration living difficulties correlated more strongly with disturbances in self-organisation (DSO) than with core PTSD symptoms.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is large but highly heterogeneous and geographically uneven. The pooled estimate should be treated as a descriptive summary rather than a generalisable prevalence. The stronger link between ongoing adversity and DSO supports the clinical relevance of the CPTSD construct in displaced populations, but causal inferences are limited by cross-sectional designs and inconsistent reporting of confounders.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CPTSD appears common in forcibly displaced people, especially among asylum seekers and those seeking care, suggesting routine screening and trauma-focused interventions are warranted; however, local prevalence may vary widely, so services should adapt to local post-migration stressors rather than rely on a single global estimate.

item.title: The effects of an online mindfulness-based intervention for parents of children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study tested whether an online mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) improves outcomes for parents of children with ADHD compared with an online psychoeducation (PSY) program. It was a two-arm RCT with 248 parents of children aged 6–12 years with ADHD symptoms.
FINDINGS: Both groups showed significant and sustained improvements in children’s ADHD symptoms, executive functioning, and parental well-being, as well as reductions in parental stress and two dimensions of expressed emotion (critical comments and initial statements). The MBI group had a small additional benefit for insomnia. A borderline improvement in parent–child relationship quality was seen in one analysis but not confirmed in sensitivity analyses.
INTERPRETATION: The trial suggests both interventions are effective, with no clear superiority of MBI except possibly for insomnia. The lack of active control for nonspecific factors (e.g., time, attention) and reliance on self-report measures limit conclusions about specific efficacy. The small effect sizes and inconsistent findings on relationship quality suggest results are preliminary and require replication with longer follow-up and objective outcomes.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Online MBIs may offer modest benefits beyond psychoeducation, particularly for sleep, but current evidence does not support replacing standard psychoeducation for parents of children with ADHD. Further trials with active controls and longer follow-up are needed before recommending routine use.

item.title: Effectiveness and Influencing Factors of Drama-Based Interventions for Social Skills in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis evaluated whether drama-based interventions improve social skills in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and explored moderators of effect size. Sixteen controlled studies with 703 participants were synthesized.
FINDINGS: Drama-based interventions produced a medium pooled effect on social skills (Hedges’ g = 0.54, 95 % CI 0.21–0.88, p = 0.002). Heterogeneity was high (I² = 76 %). Moderator analyses showed significant influences of drama approach, setting, and intervention agent, but not participant age or intervention dosage.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests a potentially useful adjunct for social-skills training in ASD, but confidence is limited by substantial heterogeneity, small-study effects not fully ruled out, and reliance on controlled rather than real-world trials. The effect size is moderate, yet variability across delivery models complicates firm conclusions about optimal implementation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Drama-based interventions may be considered as part of a broader social-skills program for autistic youth, with careful attention to the specific approach, setting, and provider to maximize benefit.

item.title: Caution before canonisation: a clinical and implementation science perspective on psychedelics.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review critically appraises the emerging evidence for psychedelic-assisted therapies (e.g., psilocybin, MDMA) in psychiatry, focusing on their therapeutic promise and methodological limitations. It synthesizes early clinical trials across depression, PTSD, and substance use disorders to assess readiness for routine care.
FINDINGS: Early trials report rapid symptom improvements under controlled conditions, but many suffer from small sample sizes (often <50 per arm), short follow-up (weeks to months), functional unblinding (due to psychoactive effects), and inconsistent safety reporting. The evidence base is preliminary, heterogeneous, and lacks comparative effectiveness against established treatments.
INTERPRETATION: The review highlights proof-of-concept efficacy but emphasizes major translational gaps: durability of effects, standardized safety protocols, and real-world feasibility. The lack of robust, long-term data and methodological rigor limits causal inference and generalizability. Ethical and implementation challenges (e.g., training, access) further complicate adoption. The findings are promising but not yet definitive.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Psychedelic therapies remain experimental; clinicians should await larger, longer, and methodologically rigorous trials before considering integration into routine care. Current evidence supports continued research but not routine use outside specialized settings.

item.title: Predicting trail-making test performance using 7-Tesla structural cerebral MRI.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study examined whether high-resolution 7-Tesla MRI-derived brain morphology (grey matter volume, cortical thickness, gyrification) can predict performance on the Trail-Making Test (TMT-A and TMT-B) in a transdiagnostic sample of 74 psychiatric patients and 41 healthy controls using a deep learning model.
FINDINGS: Prediction accuracy for TMT performance was reported as 0.795 (likely AUC). Gyrification emerged as the most influential feature in the model, with key predictive regions located in frontal, temporal, and parietal cortices. No effect sizes, confidence intervals, or p-values were provided for the predictive performance.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary and limited by the lack of statistical detail, small and diagnostically heterogeneous sample, and absence of external validation. While the reported accuracy is high, it may reflect overfitting in a single-center, cross-sectional dataset. The deep learning model’s interpretability is constrained by reliance on SHAP analysis rather than causal inference. The transdiagnostic framing is conceptually interesting but not yet clinically actionable.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, this study does not change bedside practice. It suggests a potential future role for neuroimaging-based prediction models, but current limitations in generalizability, validation, and clinical integration preclude immediate application. Further prospective, diagnostically stratified, and externally validated studies are needed.

item.title: A combined study of whole-exome sequencing and structural neuroimaging markers in bipolar disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study explores whether rare genetic variants identified via whole-exome sequencing (WES) in patients with bipolar disorder (BD) are associated with structural brain changes, addressing a gap in understanding the genetic underpinnings of BD using neuroimaging-genetic association analysis.
FINDINGS: WES was conducted on 93 BD patients and 161 healthy controls (HCs). The study identified 382 BD-related genes, including SYNE1, PKHD1L1, FRAS1, and ZFHX4, and highlighted a novel gene, GNB3, with a significant burden of rare nonsynonymous variants linked to BD. Additionally, the SNP rs56850341 in KMT2C was found to be substantially correlated with cortical thickness and white matter tract integrity in BD patients.
INTERPRETATION: This is a small, exploratory case-control study combining WES with neuroimaging, which limits generalizability and causal inference. The findings suggest potential genetic contributors to BD and brain structural changes, but the sample size is modest, and the associations require replication in larger, longitudinal cohorts. The clinical significance of these genetic variants remains uncertain without further functional validation or larger-scale studies.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Currently, these findings do not directly inform clinical practice, as the genetic variants identified are not actionable for diagnosis or treatment. Further research is needed to determine if these associations are reproducible and clinically meaningful.

item.title: "I really can't imagine anything that could've been more easy": patient perspectives on low-threshold peer-facilitated telemedicine hepatitis C treatment for people who use drugs.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study explored patient experiences of a peer-facilitated telemedicine hepatitis C (HCV) treatment model for people who use drugs (PWUD) in rural Oregon, nested within a randomized trial (Peer TeleHCV vs enhanced usual care). It used qualitative interviews to assess acceptability and perceived barriers/facilitators of this low-threshold care approach.
FINDINGS: Interviews with 34 purposively sampled participants revealed three themes: (1) staff approach and values enhanced engagement, (2) convenience and flexibility improved accessibility, and (3) practical support helped overcome care barriers. Participants described the model as accessible and supportive, emphasizing the role of peer support and telemedicine in reducing structural barriers.
INTERPRETATION: This qualitative study provides insight into patient perspectives but is limited by its small, non-random sample from a single rural setting. While findings suggest high acceptability and perceived utility of peer-facilitated telemedicine, they do not establish efficacy or generalizability. The lack of quantitative outcomes (e.g., adherence rates, SVR12) limits clinical inference. Further research is needed to determine whether these perceived benefits translate into improved treatment outcomes.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The study supports the feasibility and acceptability of peer-facilitated telemedicine for HCV treatment in rural PWUD, suggesting potential for broader implementation in substance use and infectious disease care. However, clinicians should await confirmatory evidence before adopting this model as standard practice.

item.title: A novel digital hybrid care model for maternal mental health: preliminary findings from a matched retrospective cohort study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum mood and anxiety disorders are common but often undertreated due to access barriers. This matched retrospective cohort study evaluated a hybrid digital care model (Digital Clinic) combining clinician-delivered CBT with app-based support for peripartum women with anxiety/depression.
FINDINGS: The peripartum cohort (n=13) showed a large reduction in GAD-7 scores from 14.4 (SD 5.0) to 5.5 (SD 4.3), mean change −8.9 points (p < 0.01; d = −1.91, 95% CI −2.89 to −0.93). PHQ-9 scores fell from 9.3 (SD 5.9) to 5.6 (SD 4.8), mean change −3.7 points (p = 0.055; d = −0.68, 95% CI −1.41 to 0.05).
INTERPRETATION: The study’s retrospective design, small peripartum sample, and lack of a concurrent control group limit causal inference. The large anxiety effect is statistically robust but based on a tiny cohort; depressive symptom change was not statistically significant. Funding sources and blinding status were not reported, raising potential bias risks. Larger, adequately powered RCTs are needed to confirm effectiveness and generalisability.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These preliminary findings suggest a hybrid digital model may reduce anxiety symptoms in peripartum women, but current evidence is insufficient to change routine practice; further rigorous trials are required before recommending widespread adoption.

item.title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Brain-Targeted Drug Delivery for Methamphetamine Use Disorder: Advances, Challenges and Translational Perspectives.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Methamphetamine use disorder (MUD) lacks FDA-approved pharmacotherapies, and delivering therapeutic agents to the brain is a major obstacle. This narrative review examines whether nanoparticle-mediated brain-targeted drug delivery can overcome barriers like blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and controlled release in MUD, summarizing preclinical approaches and design considerations.
FINDINGS: The review synthesizes preclinical nanotherapeutic strategies (e.g., small-molecule neuroprotectants, anti-METH vaccines, gene-silencing RNAs, neurotrophic proteins, gene-editing systems) using lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, biological, or hybrid nanocarriers. Key challenges addressed include systemic stability, BBB penetration, brain region-specific distribution, and controlled intracellular cargo release. Factors like protein corona formation, METH-induced BBB dysfunction, and neuroinflammation influence nanoparticle performance. The authors propose a systematic framework for aligning nanocarrier design with delivery obstacles and therapeutic needs, highlighting translational gaps between acute animal models and chronic human MUD.
INTERPRETATION: This is a narrative review without quantitative data (no effect sizes, p-values, or sample sizes), so the strength of evidence is low. The review provides a conceptual overview of nanomedicine’s potential in MUD but lacks critical appraisal of study quality, reproducibility, or direct clinical applicability. The proposed framework and future directions are speculative, and no safety or efficacy data in humans are presented. The translational potential remains uncertain due to disparities between preclinical models and human MUD pathology.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: No immediate clinical changes are warranted based on this review. It serves as a conceptual roadmap for future research rather than actionable clinical guidance. Clinicians should remain aware of nanomedicine as an emerging field but should not expect near-term therapeutic applications for MUD.

item.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study from the Australian Genetics of Depression Study examined whether a circadian subtype of depression—defined by ≥3 circadian features—differs clinically, pharmacologically, and genetically from non-circadian depression in 2604 adults (80% female, mean age 37.9 years).
FINDINGS: The circadian subtype (23% of participants) showed earlier onset (P<0.001), more severe symptoms (including suicidality and psychotic-like experiences, P<0.001), greater weight gain during episodes (P<0.001), and poorer self-reported response to SSRIs (OR 0.88 [95% CI 0.82–0.94]) and SNRIs (OR 0.89 [95% CI 0.83–0.97]). It was associated with higher polygenic risk for ADHD, depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, metabolic traits, inflammatory markers, and later chronotype (all P<0.05).
INTERPRETATION: The study’s cross-sectional design and self-reported outcomes limit causal inference. Selection bias (female-predominant, online-recruited sample) and lack of clinician-rated outcomes reduce external validity. The small effect sizes (ORs ~0.88–1.15) suggest limited clinical predictiveness at present. Genetic associations are hypothesis-generating and require replication.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: No immediate treatment change is warranted; the circadian subtype may flag higher symptom burden and lower SSRI/SNRI response, but evidence is preliminary. Future longitudinal studies with objective measures and clinician-rated outcomes are needed before considering tailored interventions.

item.title: From Protective Factors to Mechanisms: Charting the Neurobiology of Schizophrenia Resilience.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review explores neurobiological and psychological mechanisms that may promote resilience to schizophrenia, integrating genetic, evolutionary, and phenotypic evidence to identify potential protective factors and pathways that could inform future prevention and treatment strategies.
FINDINGS: The review highlights that common genetic variants may confer resilience by enhancing neural plasticity, fluid intelligence, and visual cognition. Candidate protective traits span obstetric, immunological, cognitive, and visual domains, though direct links to specific resilience variants remain unestablished. Evolutionary pressures may have shaped these adaptations to buffer polygenic liability for schizophrenia.
INTERPRETATION: As a narrative review, this work synthesizes emerging but preliminary evidence rather than definitive findings. The lack of direct causal links between resilience variants and mechanisms limits conclusions. The evolutionary framing is speculative, and many proposed pathways (e.g., immune or obstetric) require further validation. The discussion of neural plasticity and cognition is plausible but not yet supported by robust empirical data.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This review does not yet change clinical practice but suggests future research directions, such as targeting neural plasticity or cognitive resilience in early intervention strategies. Clinicians should remain cautious about overinterpreting these hypotheses until mechanistic and translational evidence emerges.

item.title: Dynamic gene expression signatures predict psychotherapy response in PTSD.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study investigated whether dynamic, longitudinal changes in gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) could predict psychotherapy response in veterans with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). It used a dual-state approach (unstimulated and dexamethasone-stimulated) to assess transcriptional trajectories in PTSD patients (n=17 with complete data) and controls (n=23) at pre-treatment, post-treatment, and follow-up.
FINDINGS: At pre-treatment, unstimulated responders (n=6) and non-responders (n=11) showed pronounced transcriptional differences, exceeding those between PTSD patients and controls. Longitudinally, responders shifted toward control-like gene expression profiles, while non-responders retained persistent divergence. Pathway analyses highlighted Class C/3 G-protein-coupled receptor pathways (e.g., bitter taste receptors, TAS2Rs) and subgroup-specific regulation of GABAB, opioid, and NMDA receptor signaling. Dexamethasone-induced responses further differentiated subgroups, suggesting glucocorticoid sensitivity as a predictor of treatment outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: This is a small, exploratory cohort study (n=17 PTSD patients) without randomization or blinding, limiting causal inference and generalizability. The dynamic dual-state approach is innovative but requires validation in larger, more diverse samples with standardized psychotherapy protocols. The observed transcriptional shifts in responders are intriguing but not yet clinically actionable due to the small sample size and lack of replication. The study highlights potential biomarkers (e.g., TAS2Rs, glucocorticoid sensitivity) but does not establish their predictive utility or mechanistic role in PTSD recovery.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings are preliminary and do not yet change clinical practice. They suggest that dynamic gene expression profiling *might* one day help predict psychotherapy response in PTSD, but further research is needed to confirm these signals and their clinical utility. For now, treatment decisions should rely on established clinical assessments (e.g., CAPS-5) rather than gene expression markers.

item.title: Risperidone for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and severe behavioral dysregulation: a randomized placebo-controlled assessor-blinded trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood, and treatment of children with severe behavioral dysregulation remains challenging. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adjunctive risperidone specifically in children with ADHD and clinically significant behavioral dysregulation - including irritability, impulsive aggression, and oppositional symptoms - refractory to behavioral intervention alone.

item.title: Investigating the role of drama-based strategies in addressing psychological trauma: a systematic review.
item.description: Background: Drama-based techniques have been increasingly implemented with trauma-exposed populations. However, the evidence base remains conceptually and methodologically heterogeneous, with substantial variation in how trauma is defined, how interventions are described, and which trauma-related outcomes are assessed.Objective: This review aimed to synthesise empirical studies examining drama-based interventions for individuals exposed to trauma.

item.title: Addressing heterogeneity in trauma responses in research and clinical practice: reflections and recommendations from early career researchers.
item.description: Background: There is considerable heterogeneity in how individuals respond to potentially traumatic events (PTEs). Recognising and addressing this heterogeneity has become an increasingly important focus within psychotraumatology, leading to the development of diverse research and clinical approaches.

item.title: An intervention mapping study to adapt trauma-focused social adjustment therapy for adolescents with trauma-related interpersonal difficulties.
item.description: Background: Interventions that effectively reduce posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms are not necessarily effective in improving interpersonal functioning among adolescents with complex trauma histories. Despite the developmental significance of interpersonal functioning during adolescence, there remains a lack of interventions specifically targeting trauma-related interpersonal difficulties in this population.Objective: This study aimed to adapt the Trauma-Focused Social Adjustment Therapy (TF-SAT) protocol for adolescents.

item.title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
item.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood.

item.title: Effective stimulation sites and networks for substantia nigra pars reticulata deep brain stimulation for auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia.
item.description: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNpr) is under investigation for managing auditory-verbal hallucinations (AVH) in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TR-SZ). We assessed acute AVH suppression during initial SNpr-DBS programming in three TR-SZ patients and mapped associated brain network engagement using normative connectomes. One-month post-implantation, monopolar stimulation at each electrode contact was evaluated for its effect on AVH severity.

item.title: Behavioral Health Conditions, Maternal Factors and Severe Maternal Morbidity in Michigan: A Statewide Analysis of Birth Hospitalizations.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Maternal mortality continues to rise in the United States and continued monitoring of the burden and risk factors for severe maternal morbidity (SMM) is crucial. Studies have shown that maternal substance use disorders (SUDs) and mental health disorders (i.e., behavioral health disorders (BHDs)) are important risk factors for maternal mortality, but less is known for SMM. We examined maternal characteristics and BHDs in association with SMM in Michigan (MI).

item.title: Translation and validation of a German version of the "Hopkins Competency Assessment Test," a brief method for evaluating patients' capacity to give consent.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The "Hopkins Competency Assessment Test" (HCAT) assesses a patient's ability to provide written informed consent or advance directives. It includes an essay for three reading difficulty levels (12th, 8th, and 6th school grade) and an understanding questionnaire. Currently, there is no equivalent test to the HCAT in German. Therefore, we translated, adapted, and evaluated a German version of the HCAT. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study to evaluate the psychometric properties of the HCAT in a clinical and a non-clinical sample.

item.title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy as a tool for monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes in posttraumatic stress disorder and trauma-related symptomatology: a narrative review.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in symptom presentation, illness trajectory, and treatment response, highlighting the need for objective approaches capable of monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes beyond conventional symptom-based outcomes. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an increasingly used non-invasive neuroimaging technique that enables repeated assessment of cortical hemodynamics in clinically feasible settings.

item.title: Adolescent M-CSF Administration Provides Durable Protection Against Trauma-Induced PTSD-Like Phenotypes in Male Mice Through Microglia-Dependent Mechanisms.
item.description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a severe psychiatric condition for which effective preventive strategies are lacking. Innate immune preconditioning has shown promise for the prevention of PTSD, yet the transient nature of such protection when induced in adulthood poses a substantial limitation.

item.title: Autism: epidemiology, genetics, molecular mechanisms, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. Global prevalence has risen steadily, yet reported rates vary markedly across regions and populations. These discrepancies reflect inequities in diagnostic access and screening capacity rather than true differences in incidence. This review integrates recent advances across the full ASD research spectrum. We first examine global epidemiological patterns and demographic disparities.

item.title: Hepatitis C Care Cascade in Opioid-Dependent Emergency Department Patients.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Emergency departments (ED) have become important venues for hepatitis C (HCV) screening. Similarly, EDs have had increasing engagement in the management and treatment of opioid use disorder (OUD). Persons with OUD are at disproportionate risk for acquiring HCV. We sought to assess the intersection between OUD and HCV care through observing the uptake of HCV screening and subsequent steps in the HCV care cascade in an ED-OUD cohort.

item.title: Malignant Hypertension and Thrombotic Microangiopathy Induced by Cocaine Base Paste Use: A Case Report.
item.description: Malignant hypertension (MH) and thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) are rare medical emergencies. Cocaine base paste (CBP) use has been linked in isolated cases to the simultaneous development of both conditions. We report a 41-year-old woman who developed MH complicated by TMA after intense CBP consumption. She presented with headache, visual disturbances, severe hypertension, acute kidney injury, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and moderate thrombocytopenia. Diagnosis was based on clinical and laboratory findings, without requiring plasma exchange or complement inhibitors.

item.title: Prehospital Flumazenil: Five-Year Review of Use, Indications, Outcomes, and Adverse Events in Suspected Benzodiazepine Overdose.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Historically, flumazenil was employed as both a diagnostic aid in unresponsive patients and as an antidote for suspected benzodiazepine overdose in both emergency departments and out-of-hospital settings. However, its prehospital application has been historically constrained by long-standing concerns regarding adverse events, leading many emergency medical service (EMS) systems to restrict or avoid its use. The use of flumazenil in the prehospital setting remains underreported in the literature, despite its inclusion in the treatment protocols of various EMS agencies.

item.title: Experiences of non-prescribed opioid use during opioid agonist therapy: an interpretative phenomenological analysis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Although the goal of opioid agonist therapy is typically understood by clinicians to be the cessation of the use of non-prescribed opioids, many people taking opioid agonist therapy continue to use other opioids. The purpose of this study was to explore how people who use both prescribed opioid agonist therapy and non-prescribed opioids understand their use of both agents.

item.title: Latent Profiles of Psychological Distress and Suicidal Ideation Among Nursing Students: A Cross-Sectional Study of Associated Factors.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Psychological distress and suicidal ideation frequently co-occur among nursing students, but their heterogeneity is often overlooked. OBJECTIVES: To identify latent profiles of nursing students based on psychological distress and suicidal ideation dimensions, and to explore factors associated with profile membership. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of 1461 Chinese nursing students was conducted.

item.title: Identifying capacity building priorities for implementation science in suicide prevention: a concept mapping study in Australia.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Capacity building in the science and practice of implementation is critical for driving and evaluating meaningful change. However, capacity needs of stakeholders to effectively apply implementation science in suicide prevention remain unclear. PURPOSE: To address this gap in Australia, we conducted a concept mapping (CM) study to identify and prioritize stakeholder capacity-building needs in this area.

item.title: Epidemiological comparison of cirrhosis to other long-term health conditions in the United Kingdom.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Although cirrhosis is a serious long-term health condition (LTC), it tends to receive little attention from healthcare policymakers. Here, we sought to describe how cirrhosis compares to other LTCs to inform priority-setting discussions. METHODS: We analysed data from the Our Future Health (OFH) study, a cohort of ∼1.7 million individuals from England, United Kingdom.

item.title: The Real-World Safety Profile of Haloperidol: A Comprehensive Pharmacovigilance Analysis Using the Large-Scale FAERS Database.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Haloperidol is a widely prescribed antipsychotic, but its long-term safety profile across broad populations remains insufficiently researched. Using the large-scale FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database, this study sought to comprehensively characterize the real-world adverse event profile of haloperidol and identify potential safety signals. METHODS: Adverse event reports from FAERS spanning Q1 2004 through Q1 2026, with haloperidol listed as the primary suspect drug, were analyzed.

item.title: Mapping the interplay of intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without autism spectrum disorder.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits are psychological dimensions that vary continuously across the population. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may reflect extreme expressions of these traits, yet their interdependencies and difference between typically developing (TD) children remain poorly understood. METHODS: We recruited 186 children with ASD and 364 TD children aged 6-12 years.

item.title: Urban Infrastructures of Care: Buses as Resources for Recovery and Mental Wellbeing.
item.description: Although transport infrastructures are increasingly recognised as determinants of urban wellbeing, their role in trajectories of becoming well and becoming ill has received little empirical and theoretical attention, particularly in serious mental ill-health. This paper examines how bus infrastructures function as everyday resources and obstacles for people living with psychosis.

item.title: [Dissociative psychosis induced by combat stress: A clinical case].
item.description: In contemporary contexts, there is a noticeable rise in the prevalence of psychogenic mental disorders among military personnel subjected to combat stress. This article presents a rare clinical case of psychogenic psychosis in a serviceman that emerged as a result of combat-related stress. It details the significance of the case, the primary pathogenetic factors involved (such as severe psychological trauma and premorbid sensitivity), the characteristics of the disorder (including acute onset, disorientation, pseudodementia, and puerilism), and the patient's response to treatment.

item.title: Women With Bipolar Disorder are at Increased Risk of Sarcopenia.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: While bipolar disorder is associated with significant comorbidity, little is known about the musculoskeletal health of individuals with bipolar disorder. Thus, we aimed to investigate the association between bipolar disorder and muscle strength, mass, quality and sarcopenia. METHODS: Women with bipolar disorder (n = 106) were recruited from healthcare settings and age-matched to controls (n = 300), without bipolar disorder, from the Geelong Osteoporosis Study. Both groups, aged ≥ 20 years. were drawn from South-Eastern Australia.

item.title: [Autism, selective mutism and mild intellectual disability explained by 17q12 microdeletion syndrome].
item.description: The patient had presented symptoms during preschool years with motor coordination difficulties, deviant reactions to sensory stimuli and separation anxiety. A language stagnation had occurred at the age of 1.5 to 2 years. At school start, she became completely mute during school hours but spoke at home. At assessment at the Child Neuropsychiatric Clinic at the age of 10, autism, selective mutism and ADHD/ADD were diagnosed. Her intellectual level corresponded to borderline intellectual functioning, and a similar test result was evident also at the age of 14 years.

item.title: Association Between Neighborhood Characteristics and Parent-Reported Lifetime History of Concussion Among Adolescents in the United States.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Examine the association between neighborhood characteristics and parent-reported lifetime concussion history. SETTING: National Survey of Children's Health, a nationally representative survey of parents of children ages 0-17 years in the United States. PARTICIPANTS: Parent/guardian(s) (hereafter: parents) with children ages 0-17 years. DESIGN: Cross-sectional.

item.title: Neurodevelopmental Conditions Amongst Care-Experienced Children: A Population-Based Cohort Study Using Linked Health, Social Care, and Education Records from Wales.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Care-experienced children are a vulnerable group with higher exposure to inequalities. Nationwide evidence on the proportion of children with neurodevelopmental conditions (NDCs) and age at diagnosis among those with care experience is limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales. NDCs were identified using healthcare and education records among a cohort of children born between 2002 and 2006, followed to age 16.

item.title: Aging in Autism: An Event-Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection.
item.description: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors. Mismatch negativity and the P3a component are event-related potentials (ERPs) indexing automatic auditory change detection and involuntary attention shift.

item.title: Parabacteroides distasonis ameliorates methylphenidate hydrochloride-induced colonic inflammatory responses and associated gastrointestinal distress.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood, with methylphenidate hydrochloride (MPH) as its first-line pharmacotherapy. Though effective, MPH is associated with underrecognized gastrointestinal adverse events warranting further investigation. Recently, the gut microbiota has attracted attention for treating gastrointestinal distress, but research on its role in alleviating MPH-induced gastrointestinal reactions remains scarce.

item.title: Screen use, parent-child interaction, and social interaction behaviors in autistic children.
item.description: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed children's everyday environments, raising concerns about excessive screen use and its potential developmental implications. Although research on screen use has increased substantially, relatively little is known about how screen use may relate to family interaction processes among autistic children. The present study aimed to examine the relationships among screen use, autism severity, parent-child interaction behaviors, and children's social interaction behaviors in autistic children.

item.title: Working memory and language development have a bi-directional longitudinal relationship in autistic preschoolers.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Among neurotypical children working memory and language development are closely related, but the longitudinal relationship between these factors is unknown in autism. This study had the goal of evaluating potential bidirectional relationships between these domains. METHODS: A longitudinal design included language and visuospatial working memory assessments across three time points with 160 autistic preschoolers. Time points were one year apart.
